zh.facts: 费马测试的塔罗牌测试有22道原创情境题，约7分钟，免注册。答完可免费看22张大阿卡纳主题的选择次数和全部最高结果。公开指南可以直接阅读。
zh.intro: 如果要开启一个小项目，你会先试一小步、把手边的材料用起来，还是先定一个方向？用约 7 分钟答完 22 道情境题，看看你的选择更常落在哪张塔罗牌的主题。免费查看完整结果。
deliverables: 查看 22 张牌的选择次数
每题为所选主题加 1，合计 22。所有同为最高的结果都会保留。
免费读全部大阿卡纳指南
22 张牌各有指南，解释与日常具体选择的关联。无需先提交答卷。
单项最高可复制牌名和指南；并列时会复制全部最高牌名与入口。链接不带答案或次数。
interpretations: 这份样张每逢愚人选项就选择先试小一步。4 代表选中四次。

全选 A，22 张牌各 1 次

fool: 你较常选留一点好奇，再迈出小步。

lovers: 说出在乎的事，再一起选
你较常选把双方愿意和不愿意的条件讲清楚。

你较常选先独自整理思路，再决定是否讨论。
收到几份提案后，你先自己读一遍，记下想问的地方再去开会。
wheel-of-fortune: 看看有哪些条件已经变了
你较常选重新分清新情况与自己的选择。

justice: 把事实、推测和约定分开
你较常选先核对信息，再讨论怎样分配才合适。
小组对分工有分歧时，你把实际任务量列出来，再一起调整。
hanged-man: 你较常选留一个复盘点，试试从别处想同一个问题。

你较常选挑一部分做组合，并观察哪些条件要调整。

tower: 确认哪条假设不管用了
你较常选遇到错位时返回检查，再决定修整局部还是换安排。

你较常选看见限制后，保留一个可选的小机会。

moon: 把看到的和想到的分开
你较常选保留疑问，避免用想象填多余的空白。

sun: 留意这一刻具体哪里好
你较常选给普通生活里的愉快留一点时间。
下班路上听到一首喜欢的歌，你站一会儿听完，再慢慢回家。
judgement: 回头看看已知条件，再选一次
你较常选区分当时与现在知道的事，再改一个具体决定。

world: 你较常选确认一段工作完成，再决定哪些问题留给以后。

faq: 要先抽牌或填生日吗？
无需抽牌、生日或塔罗背景。结果来自你对 22 道原创题的选择。
为什么只有大阿卡纳？
这套题本以 22 张大阿卡纳作主题，不包含其余 56 张小阿卡纳。
22 道题怎么计数？
每题四选一，选到哪张主题就加 1。每张出现 4 次，单项 0–4，合计 22。最高并列全部保留。
死神、高塔和恶魔是不好的结果吗？
这三个主题分别对应日常收尾、重新核对假设，以及区分愿望与限制。结果不预测死亡、灾祸或好坏。
结果能判断性格或恋爱命运吗？
这份娱乐题只统计具体选择，没有心理测量或关系预测依据，也不能换算为 MBTI 或大五。
分享会附带作答记录或图片吗？
分享只复制公开牌名与指南或测试入口，不附答案、次数、个人标识或个人 PNG。
zh.formula: 22 题四选一，每次给所选主题加 1。每张牌出现 4 次，在 A、B、C、D 各一次，单卡 0–4，合计 22。全部并列最高都会显示。

deliverables: 每題替一個主題記 1 次，合計 22。所有並列最高的牌都會列出。
免費讀 22 篇公開指南

interpretations: 這份範例在四次看到這項做法時，都選了帶著好奇先試一小步。

一路選 A，22 張牌都是 1 次

fool: 你比較常選先做個小嘗試，再看自己還想不想繼續。

設計圖越改越亂時，你去走一小段路，回來把它當成第一次看。

faq: 需要出生日期、抽牌或塔羅知識嗎？
都不用。結果來自 22 道情境題的選擇。
為什麼只列大阿爾克那牌？

22 道題怎麼計次？
每題四選一，替選到的牌加 1。每張牌出現 4 次，每項 0–4，合計 22，同為最高的都會保留。
死神、高塔和惡魔代表壞事嗎？

轉傳會附答案或個人圖卡嗎？

en.facts: FermatMind’s Which Tarot Card Are You quiz uses 22 original scenarios and takes about seven minutes. It is free without registration. Results show counts for 22 Major Arcana themes and keep every tie for the highest count. All 22 public guides are available to read before answering. The quiz requires no birth date, random draw, or prior knowledge of tarot.
en.intro: At the start of a small project, do you try one simple step, make something with what you have, or decide on a direction? Choose how you would respond in 22 original scenarios and see which Major Arcana themes appear most in your choices. The full result is free.
deliverables: Each choice adds one, for a total of 22. The result keeps every card theme tied for the highest count.
Every Major Arcana theme has its own public guide. You can read any of them before taking the quiz.
Share a public guide or quiz link
One highest result shares its name and guide. A tie shares all leading names and the public quiz. Links carry no answers or counts.
interpretations: The sample chose every option that favored a curious first step. Four represents four selections.
The Magician and The Hermit tie at 4 each
Both guides appear. Compare making a quick sample from available materials with setting aside time to think independently.
Every card appears once in position A, so all 22 guides appear. Revisit the situations to understand your choices.

fool: You often chose an easy first step that leaves room for curiosity.
At a pottery class, you try shaping the base before deciding whether to make a whole cup.
magician: Make something with what is at hand
You often chose to turn available materials into a visible first version.
When a frame is unavailable, you make a cardboard sample to check the size.
high-priestess: You often chose to set aside an impression until there was more to go on.
After a short reply from a friend, you note what you still want to ask and wait until you meet.
empress: Make room for something to grow
You often chose to consider time, materials, and how much care you could offer.
Before planting mint, you look for sunlight and decide how often you can water it.
emperor: Make a structure people can use
You often chose to clarify scope, order, and how people will share resources.
When several people share a desk, you write a schedule with a space for changes.
hierophant: Find out why a practice is used
You often chose to learn where a familiar method came from before passing it on.
While learning a family recipe, you ask which steps affect the texture and which can change.
lovers: Say what matters before choosing together
You often chose to share preferences and check what everyone was willing to do.
When planning a weekend, you say you would like a walk and ask whether a friend would prefer an exhibition.
chariot: Pick the next step you can finish
You often chose a direction with a clear point to review it.
While assembling an album, you decide to choose ten photos before deciding whether to add more.
strength: Speak gently and keep a clear limit
You often chose to state what you could do without leaving the limits unspoken.
When asked to pick up extra work, you say you have one hour and explain what someone else would need to do.
hermit: Take a little time to think alone
You often chose to organize your thoughts before deciding what to discuss.
Before a meeting, you read the plans on your own and write down the questions to bring.
wheel-of-fortune: Notice what has changed around you
You often chose to check the new circumstances before making another decision.
When a favored café turns out to be closed, you check its opening days before moving the meetup.
justice: Check the facts before deciding what is fair
You often chose to separate evidence from assumptions and agreements.
When a group disagrees about who did what, you list the actual tasks before changing the division.
hanged-man: Pause and look from another angle
You often chose to step back and revisit an awkward situation from a different point of view.
When revisions make a poster confusing, you take a walk and then look at it with fresh eyes.
death: You often chose to decide which parts of a finished project could be put away.
When an event is over, you save the reusable documents and archive the rest of the plan.
temperance: Try blending two approaches on a small scale
You often chose to test a combination before using it everywhere.
With two kinds of paper left, you make a tiny collage to see how well they go together.
devil: Name what you want and what limits it
You often chose to distinguish a wish from a commitment or practical constraint.
Before signing up for two classes, you compare the cost and the time actually available each week.
tower: Recheck the assumption that no longer fits
You often chose to find what was wrong with the existing plan before changing it.
When bookings keep clashing, you discover that people read the time differently and fix the shared calendar.
star: Leave room for something still possible
You often chose to acknowledge a limit while keeping an option available.
After an outdoor event is canceled, you keep one part of the plan in mind for another day.
moon: Separate what you saw from what you imagined
You often chose to mark what you knew, what you suspected, and what still needed checking.
When you hear a date may have changed, you check with the organizer before telling the group.
sun: You often chose to spend a little time on something genuinely enjoyable.
On the way home, you stop to listen to a favorite song before carrying on.
judgement: Review what you know and choose again
You often chose to see what had changed and revise one decision.
After an event, you realize newcomers missed the entrance and add a map to the next invitation.
world: You often chose to decide which part of a task was complete and could be left to rest.
When an album is ready, you save the chosen version and keep the unused pictures in their folder.

faq: Do I need a birth date, card draw, or tarot knowledge?
No. The score comes from choices in 22 everyday scenarios.
Why are only Major Arcana included?
This quiz uses the 22 Major Arcana themes. The other 56 cards in the familiar deck are outside its scope.
How are the 22 answers counted?
Your choice adds one to one card. Each card appears four times, for a count of 0–4. The total is 22, and every highest tie stays.
Are Death, the Tower, and the Devil bad results?
They represent ordinary endings, checking assumptions, and distinguishing wants from limits. They do not predict death, disasters, or bad luck.
Can my result tell me my personality or relationship future?
It counts choices on an entertainment quiz. It does not predict relationship outcomes, assess personality, or convert to MBTI or Big Five.
Will sharing include answers or a personal card?
Sharing copies public names and links without answers, counts, private IDs, or a personal PNG.
en.formula: Choose one of four options per scenario. Each choice adds one to its card theme. Each card appears four times, once in each answer position, giving counts of 0–4 and a total of 22. Every highest tie appears.
en.boundary: Museum sources document tarot’s history and the structure of a deck. Waite’s historical text explains the ordering used here, with Strength VIII and Justice XI. FermatMind wrote the scenarios. Results record choices without drawing cards, predicting events, or providing a psychological assessment.
